label: Transaction Status
title: Transaction Status
summary: Use a Transaction Status for the state and date of one payment on one line, as at the foot of a Transaction Bubble.
corePrinciple: One word for the state; the mode colours the mark.

anatomy.title: A mark and one line of text
anatomy.description: An 18 px mark, then the status and the date as one line of text, joined by a middle dot.
blocks: 18 px; the mode picks a tick, a cross, or “!”, and its colour.
status, a middle dot, then date: one text on one line.
No width of its own: as wide as its words.

configuration.title: Four modes, any words
configuration.description: The Transaction Status mode sets the mark, as in Figma: Request an orange “!”, Paid a green tick, Declined a red cross, and Expired, the default, a grey “!”. status and date are free text that the mode doesn’t change, so set the word and the mode together.
blocks: An orange “!”: a request still waiting.
A green tick: the money went through.
A red cross: the bank turned it down.
A grey “!”: the request ran out.

states.title: One line, or wrapped
states.description: The line has no states of its own: it doesn’t press, select, or load. In a column narrower than the words, it ellipsizes at the end, so the date goes first; disableTruncation lets it wrap instead. Both examples sit in a 200 px column.
blocks: The date is cut; the mark keeps its 18 px.
The date moves to a second line.

sizing.title: 18 px tall, as wide as its words
sizing.description: The line is 18 px tall: an 18 px mark, 4 px of space, then 12 px text on a 16 px line. It has no width of its own and grows with its words. A narrower column, or a Transaction Bubble, cuts them at the end, and the mark keeps its 18 px.

content.title: One word and a short date
content.description: Write status as one word that matches the mode: Requested, Paid, Declined, or Expired. Write date short, such as 21 Oct 2026, or Today for a recent payment; the line adds the middle dot. Request and Expired share the “!” mark, so the word has to say which.
blocks: A recent payment can say Today.

examples.description: A recent payment can say Today.

inContext.title: On the payments in a thread
inContext.description: Every Transaction Bubble ends with a Transaction Status. Set the Transaction Status mode on the bubble, as in Figma: the bubble passes its modes to the line, and its status and date props give the words.

doDont.description: Each pair shows a line people read correctly next to one whose colour or length works against it.

sources.title: Use the public Transaction Status contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma subcomponent with the installed package and its Storybook story.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. In Figma, Transaction Status is a subcomponent (Coin Subcomponents) with no properties: its mode picks the icon, the colour, and the word together. In the package the mode picks the mark’s icon and colour, as in Figma, and status and date are free text; with no mode it is Expired: a grey “!” beside “Expired”. Figma’s line ends in a chevron; in the package the chevron belongs to Transaction Bubble. When the words don’t fit a column or a Transaction Bubble, they end in an ellipsis and the mark keeps its 18 px.
